title: German Dark Rye Bread
directions: In a large mixing bowl pour in hot coffee. Stir in shortening, molasses and salt and continue stirring until shortening melts.
In a smaller bowl pour in lukewarm water. Sprinkle yeast over water and let stand 10 minutes. Stir with a fork and add to coffee mixture.
Beat in by hand or with an electric mixer 3 cups (750 mL) flour and 2 cups (500 mL) rye flour. Then by hand add remaining flours, working the last portion in with a rotating motion of the hand.

Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead 8 to 10 minutes. Shape into a smooth ball and place in a deep greased bowl, rotating ball to cover with grease. Cover with a damp cloth and in a warm place allow to rise 1 1/2 times original size (about 1 1/2 hours).
Punch down, shape into 3 round loaves. Roll each loaf in oat bran to garnish the top. Place on greased cookie sheets, cover and allow to rise again 1 1/2 times in volume (about 1 hour).
Bake in a 400° F (200° C) oven for 30 minutes or until hollow sounding when tapped.
notes: Printed newspaper clipping with holly decoration (Christmas issue). Intro: 'From the Purity Cookbook this round loaf is a warm accompaniment to our savory oyster stew.'
raw_text:
GERMAN DARK RYE BREAD
From the Purity Cookbook this round loaf is a warm accompaniment to our savory oyster stew.
2 cups  hot strong coffee  500 mL
1/4 cup  shortening  50 mL
2/3 cup  molasses  150 mL
1 Tbsp.  salt  15 mL
2 tsp.  sugar  10 mL
1 cup  lukewarm water  250 mL
2 Tbsp.  active dry yeast  25 mL
5 cups  flour  1250 mL
4 cups  dry rye flour  1 L
1/4 cup  oat bran  50 mL
In a large mixing bowl pour in hot coffee. Stir in shortening, molasses and salt and continue stirring until shortening melts.
In a smaller bowl pour in lukewarm water. Sprinkle yeast over water and let stand 10 minutes. Stir with a fork and add to coffee mixture.
Beat in by hand or with and electric mixer 3 cups (750 mL) flour and 2 cups (500 mL) rye flour. Then by hand add remaining flours, working the last portion in with a rotating motion of the hand.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead 8 to 10 minutes. Shape into a smooth ball and place in a deep greased bowl, rotating ball to cover with grease. Cover with a damp cloth and in a warm place allow to rise 1 1/2 times original size (about 1 1/2 hours). Punch down, shape into 3 round loaves. Roll each loaf in oat bran to garnish the top. Place on greased cookie sheets, cover and allow to rise again 1 1/2 times in volume (about 1 hour). Bake in a 400° F (200° C) oven for 30 minutes or until hollow sounding when tapped.

title: Hot Cross Buns
directions: Combine 1st 4 ingred & 2 c flour. In saucepan heat milk & marg to 120-130°.
With mixer on low beat liquid into dry ingred. At med. speed beat 2 min. Beat in peel, 3 eggs, 1 1/2 c flour, beat 2 min.
Stir in raisins & 2 c flour. On floured surface, knead dough till smooth & elastic, working in 1/2 c flour.
Shape into ball, place in greased bowl. Cover let rise. Punch down. Cut into 24 pcs. Cover let rest 15 min.
Grease 13x9" bk pan. Shape into balls place in pan. Cover, let rise. Beat remaining egg. Cut cross in bun brush c egg.
Bake @ 375° for 20-25 min. Cool in pan - In bowl mix confec. sugar & 1 tbsp H2O - pipe across each bun.
notes: Back of Hot Cross Buns card (photo 209).

ENGLISH MUFFIN CHEESE LOAF
1 tsp Sugar
1/4 c lukewarm water
1 Tbsp. yeast
1 c milk
1 tsp. Salt
2 1/2 c flour
1 tsp. dry mustard
1/4 tsp. baking soda
3/4 c grated cheddar cheese
2 Tbsp. cornmeal

title: English Muffin Cheese Loaf
directions: In lrg. bowl, dissolve sugar in water. Sprinkle yeast over & let stand 10 min.
In saucepan combine milk & salt. Scald & let cool to lukewarm. Add to dissolved yeast.
Add 1 c flour, mustard, baking soda & cheese; mix until smooth. Stir in remaining flour.
Grease 8x4" loaf pan & dust c cornmeal. Place dough in pan & sprinkle with cornmeal. Cover & let rise in warm place for aprox. 45 min.
Bake in 400° oven for 25 min. Remove from pan & cool on rack.
notes: - recipe may be doubled.
